messages.content: What is the largest planet in the universe?

function.name: space_star_info

message.content:
The largest planet that has been confirmed so far is **HD 100546 b**.  
It orbits the young B‑type star HD 100546 and has a radius of roughly **2.5 × Jupiter’s radius** (about 180,000 km). Its mass is estimated at around **10–15 M_J**, making it one of the most massive “hot Jupiters” known.

Other very large exoplanets include:

| Planet | Mass (≈ M_J) | Radius (≈ R_J) |
|--------|--------------|----------------|
| HD 106906 b | ~11 | ~1.5 |
| WASP‑17 b | ~0.5 | ~1.8 |
| Kepler‑39 b | ~20 | ~1.0 |

These values are derived from radial‑velocity and transit measurements, and they represent the upper end of the planetary mass spectrum observed to date.
